title: Match a customer's payment
summary: How to mark an invoice paid when the customer's money arrives in your bank, including part payments and one deposit for several invoices.

sections.heading: Match a deposit to its invoice

steps.text: Bring in your bank file, and open To review.
A deposit that pays an invoice shows Invoice and the invoice, such as INV-1061 · Harbourview Developments, and why: its number is in the description, or it is the amount owed.

image.description: A deposit in To review, DEPOSIT HARBOURVIEW DEVELOPMENTS INV 1061, $4,180.00, showing Invoice, INV-1061 · Harbourview Developments, its number is in the description, Split across invoices, Choose an account instead, and the button Match.

steps.text: Check it is the right invoice, then click Match. The deposit is posted, and the invoice shows Paid with the date the money arrived.
If it is not an invoice payment, click Choose an account instead, and post it as usual.
Click Split across invoices under the deposit. Every invoice still owing is listed.

image.description: The sheet Split $2,640.00 across invoices: INV-1063, INV-1062 and INV-1064 with what each owes and a Paying now box. $2,640.00 is typed for INV-1062, and Left to split says $0.00 with a tick.

steps.text: Type what the deposit pays on each invoice in Paying now. A part payment leaves the rest of that invoice owing.
If the customer paid more than they owe, choose an account in The rest goes to.
When Left to split says $0.00 with a tick, click Save split.

sections.heading: If something goes wrong
paragraphs: You matched the wrong invoice: click Undo in the message at the top, or press Command and Z. The invoice is owed again, and the deposit waits in To review.
Save split stays grey: the amounts do not add up to the deposit, or one is more than that invoice owes. Left to split says what is wrong.
No invoice is suggested: the invoice may not be in your books yet. Bring it in from the Admin Dashboard first, then come back to the deposit.
